headline: KTBs ignore a 4.4% KOSPI rebound and a 2bp Treasury rise: foreign futures buying and falling oil pull the 10Y down 1.3bp to 3.850% and the 30Y 1.8bp, while hike pricing lifts the 2Y 1.4bp and inverts 2s3s for the first time this year
summary: KTBs firmed beyond the 2Y in a bull flattener even as KOSPI jumped 4.4%: the 3Y fell 0.6bp to 3.633%, the 10Y 1.3bp to 3.850% and the 30Y 1.8bp to 3.959%, while the 2Y rose 1.4bp to 3.643%, leaving 2s3s at −1.0bp and 3s10s at 21.7bp, both 1-year lows. Month to date the 10Y is −15.8bp and the 3Y −8.2bp, but on the week the 2Y is +4.2bp and the 3Y +2.0bp as a November 26 hike stays priced. Bills kept grinding higher: CD rose 1bp to 3.37%, a fresh 1-year high, CP held at 3.83% and MSB 91-day at 3.174% (96th percentile), while MSB 2Y rose 0.7bp to 3.658%, 1.5bp over KTB. Spread products were steady to firmer: KDB 3Y 21bp over KTB (−1.5bp), AAA bank 1Y 42.5bp (93rd percentile), AA- 3Y 69bp (88th) and KEPCO 3Y 44bp, still within 2bp of its 1-year wide.
drivers: Foreign futures buying and cheaper oil beat the equity rebound

Bonds opened weaker as KOSPI gapped up, then rallied as foreigners bought 11,296 3Y and 2,284 10Y futures, extending buying that has run since October (they bought KRW 8.45tn of Korean bonds in October, per KOFIA, after net selling in September). WTI has dropped from above USD 100 early this month to about USD 85 on hopes of US–Iran de-escalation, which dealers said the long end is now pricing. The 10Y future rose 9 ticks to 109.48, 1 tick over our basket fair value of 109.47 (on fair), while the 3Y rose 2 ticks to 103.83, 9 ticks (about 3bp) below its 103.92 fair value for a second day, so the cheapness stays at the front end.
US Treasuries: a 2bp rise that KTBs ignored

In New York on Monday the US 10Y par yield rose 2bp to 4.88% and the 2Y 5bp to 4.56% as stocks rebounded and the USD 58bn 3Y auction tailed (4.627%, bid-to-cover 2.53, the lowest since mid-2025). At the 1-year daily beta of 0.46 that implied +0.9bp for the KTB 10Y against an actual −1.3bp, so the day was a 2.2bp local rally against the global move. The KTB–UST 10Y gap widened to −103bp, a new 1-year extreme, ahead of US October CPI tonight (consensus +0.3% m/m headline, +0.2% core) with about 80% of a December Fed hike priced.

KOSPI rose 4.39% to 5,239.13 (intraday 5,300.92, buy sidecar at the open) on a US chip rally, its first gain in four sessions, and foreigners bought about KRW 0.35tn of stock, their first net purchase in eight sessions; Samsung Electronics rose 4.7% and SK hynix 6.7%. The won firmed 9.6 to 1,337.5 per dollar. One day of buying does not end the rotation: margin credit was flat at KRW 28.1tn and the bond market treated the bounce as relief rather than a turn.
Hike pricing holds the 1–2Y; BOK minutes back it after the close

The 2Y rose 1.4bp and MSB 2Y 0.7bp while the 3Y fell, inverting 2s3s to −1.0bp (average 13bp) and keeping 1s2s at 7.3bp, a 1st-percentile reading, and CD set another 1-year high at 3.37%. Minutes of the October 22 hold, released after the close, showed a unanimous hold at 3.00% but several members arguing to keep the tightening stance and judge the timing and size of further hikes on conditions, which supports the November 26 hike to 3.25% the bill curve already prices.

view: Today showed the local bid is real: the KTB 10Y fell 1.3bp while Treasuries implied +0.9bp and KOSPI rose 4.4%, and over four weeks the 10Y is −33bp, of which −13bp is US Treasuries at a weekly beta of 0.58 and −20bp is Korea's own rotation. The weekly rotation signal is +1.37 (daily +1.80) and stays in the bond-rally regime because a one-day KOSPI rebound has not reversed the 7.6% four-week drop, the 13% fall in margin credit or foreigners' futures buying. The front end is still the weak spot, with the 2Y at 3.64% fully pricing a November 26 hike to 3.25% and 2s3s inverted, so gains have to come from the belly and long end. I expect the 10Y to hold 3.78–3.95% into the BOK meeting; I would not chase below 3.85% and would buy 3.95–4.00%, with tonight's US CPI and the 10Y/30Y auctions the main swing factors at about 0.4–0.5bp per Treasury bp. I stay flat the curve until KOSPI holds its rebound for a week. The signal's record remains better against Treasuries (hedged rally calls right 67% of the time and sell-off calls 69%, against 50% and 57% outright; Sharpe 1.32 vs 1.00), so a KTB 10Y long against about 0.6 × US 10Y is still the cleaner expression than outright duration, with the record −103bp KTB–UST gap the main cost.

buckets.name: KTB 1–2Y front end
buckets.why: The 2Y rose 1.4bp to 3.643%, 64th percentile of its 1-year range (average 3.37%), and is +4.2bp on the week; the 1Y is 3.570% (86th). 1s2s is 7.3bp (1st percentile, average 30bp) and 2s3s inverted to −1.0bp, a 1-year low (average 13bp). MSB 91-day 3.174% (96th) and CD 3.37% (1-year high) price a November 26 hike to 3.25% and a 3.50% terminal, and the October minutes back that.
buckets.call: Not triggered: the 2Y stayed above 3.60%. Keep: fade a close below 3.60% (target 3.70%, stop 3.52%); add above 3.80%.

buckets.name: 3s10s curve
buckets.why: 3s10s flattened 0.7bp to 21.7bp, a new 1-year low (0th percentile, average 40bp), as the long end rallied on foreign futures buying and oil despite KOSPI's 4.4% jump. Our steepener from 29bp was stopped on Nov 5; the curve has since kept flattening, so the stop was right.
buckets.call: Stay flat. KOSPI's rebound is one day old; re-enter the steepener (3 × 3Y vs 1 × 10Y futures) only once it holds a week, then target 30bp, stop 18bp.

buckets.name: KTB 10Y outright
buckets.why: The 10Y at 3.850% is at the 45th percentile of a 3.20–4.60% range (average 3.90%), −15.8bp month to date and −54bp since the rally call on Oct 8. Today's −1.3bp came against a +0.9bp Treasury-implied move, a 2.2bp local rally; the KTB–UST gap of −103bp is the widest of the year, leaving little cushion if US CPI or auctions push Treasuries up.
buckets.call: Buy zone 3.95–4.00% not reached; keep it, stop 4.10%, target 3.80%. Don't chase below 3.85%.

buckets.name: Ultra-long 30–50Y
buckets.why: 30s50s widened 0.7bp to +3.2bp, 98th percentile (average −9.3bp), as the 30Y (−1.8bp) beat the 50Y (−1.1bp), so the switch from +2.5bp is 0.7bp against. The 10s20s30s fly rose 2.5bp to 14.5bp (81st) with the 20Y lagging. On Monday's trades the 30Y benchmark 26-8 (154 trades) sat on the curve, 26-2 2056 was 2.5bp cheap and 19-6 2039 6.6bp rich.
buckets.call: Keep the 30Y into 50Y switch from +2.5bp; target −3bp, stop +6bp. Open, 0.7bp against.

buckets.name: KDB 1–3Y vs KTB
buckets.why: The KDB fit (26 trades) puts the 3Y 21.3bp over KTB, −1.5bp today, 60th percentile (average 19bp), so the overweight from about 26bp is 4.7bp in favour and 1.3bp from target. The 1Y fit is 33bp over (89th) and KOFIA's 1Y KDB quote 30bp (79th, average 24bp). KEXIM has only 3 trades (low confidence), so ignore its 39bp readings.
buckets.call: Hold from ~26bp; take profit at 20bp. Tighten the stop to 28bp (from 35bp) to lock in most of the gain.

buckets.name: AAA bank debentures and money market
buckets.why: AAA bank paper (60-trade fit) is 42.5bp over the 1Y KTB, 93rd percentile (average 31bp), and 38.6bp at 2Y (94th). CD rose 1bp to 3.37%, a 1-year high, and CP held at 3.83%, so CP–CD is 46bp (92nd, average 28bp). IBK 1Y (19 trades) is 32bp over, 77th percentile.
buckets.call: No change: prefer KDB over bank debentures; revisit bank paper once CP–CD falls below 35bp.

buckets.name: Corporate credit (AA- 3Y)
buckets.why: AA- 3Y fell 0.5bp to 4.327%, so the spread is 69bp (88th percentile, average 61bp); KEPCO 3Y at 44bp over is the 98th percentile (wide 46bp, average 34bp) and BBB- minus AA- is 583bp (73rd). KOFIA data show demand in October shifted to AA and above while A-rated book-building participation fell sharply, so lower grades remain the weak spot.
buckets.call: Add AA- only above 75bp or once KOSPI holds a rebound for a week; no trigger hit.

watch: Next: US October CPI tonight (Nov 10, 22:30 KST) and the US 10Y auction (results about 03:00 KST Nov 11), the US Veterans Day bond holiday and Korea's November 1–10 exports on Nov 11, the US 30Y auction on Nov 12, the college entrance exam on Nov 19 (KRX opens an hour late), then the BOK meeting on Nov 26 and the FOMC on Dec 8–9; a hot CPI would hit KTBs at about 0.4–0.5bp per Treasury bp, while KOSPI holding its rebound with foreigners buying stocks is the local risk to the rally.
